column1: # schemas.tsv (harbor#1424) — the schema of every .tsv register: its columns, key, references, owner and reader.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A register's columns were declared in a comment, a header row, or nowhere, and 111 scripts
# found a column by counting tabs, so a column added in the middle shifted every reader silently. One row per register
# says what it holds; bin/standard-register.sh reads any register BY NAME through its row, and judges the tree both ways:
# a tracked .tsv with no row is red, a row with no file is red (standard.register-declared), and a reference column
# holding an id absent from its target is red (standard.reference-resolves). A register is its file plus its row here.
# COLUMNS  id <TAB> header <TAB> columns <TAB> key <TAB> refs <TAB> owner <TAB> read_by <TAB> note
#   id        the register's path from the repo root, or a glob with one * (it stands for a name within one directory); a trailing ?
#             says the file may be absent (a repo's own overlay, or a dev-layer file the core export does not ship), and every other row
#             names a file the tree must hold
#   header    row when the first data line is a header row that must equal `columns`; none when the file has no header
#             row (its columns are declared only here); = on a copy
#   columns   the column names in order. A name ending in ? is optional and trailing. =<path> says the file is a copy
#             of that register, a * standing for the name the glob matched (a vendored register): header, columns and key
#             are the original's and its references are judged there
#   key       the column, or columns joined with +, that is unique per row; - when no column is
#   refs      space-separated <column>><target>: <target> is <register path>:<column> (the value must be a row's) or
#             path:<prefix> (the value, after the prefix, must be a path in the tree); @<sep> after it splits a cell into
#             several ids (@space for a blank); |<value> allows a literal. An empty cell and - are never references
#   owner     the family that answers for it (terms.tsv, class family)
#   read_by   the engine that reads it, or - when none does
# SCOPE. A register is every tracked *.tsv outside a fixtures/ directory and outside a directory or file named test*.
# A repo that vendors the naming package declares its own registers in naming-schemas.tsv at its root, same shape.
